38: Disrupts the ship's shields after firing this weapon, allowing damage from hostile weapons to "leak through" to the hull even if shields are up. Shield disruption wears off over time, but imparting disruption on yourself does not lose effectiveness as your shields become more leaky.
39: Reduces shields for some time after this weapon is fired.
40: Reduces hull for some time after this weapon is fired.
41: Reduces fuel for some time after this weapon is fired.
42: Increases heat for some time after this weapon is fired.
43: Energy consumed per second, as a percentage of your total energy capacity.
44: Increases your heat as a percentage of your maximum heat capacity by this amount per second.
45: Fuel used or lost per second as a percentage of the ship's total fuel.
46: Hull damage dealt to your ship per second, as a percentage of your total hull strength.
47: Shield damage dealt to your ship per second, as a percentage of your total shield strength.
48: Projectiles fired per second by this weapon. Weapons that fire continuously do not require batteries if the ship's energy generation per second is higher than the weapon's firing energy per second. Some continuous fire weapons only fire a fraction of the time, in which case the ship's energy production must be higher than the weapon's firing energy divided by the firing time to not require batteries.
49: Degrees this turret can turn per second.
50: Modifies the turret turn rate on this ship by the given factor.
51: The angular range of protection provided by this weapon, in degrees.
52: How this projectile tracks its target. Projectiles with "direct" will fly straight at their target, while projectiles with "leading" will lead their trajectory.
53: This projectile's ability to maintain its target lock.
54: This projectile's ability to maintain an optical target lock, which depends on the size of the target; negatively affected by any potential optical jamming equipment.
55: This projectile's ability to maintain an infrared target lock, which depends on the target ship's heat level and distance from the missile; IR-guided missiles become more accurate the closer they are to their targets.
56: This projectile's ability to maintain a radar target lock; negatively affected by the target ship's radar jamming equipment.
59: Damage dealt to minable objects per shot, in lieu of hull damage.
60: Fuel lost by the target per shot when hit by this weapon. Only half as effective when the target's shields are up. A negative amount means fuel is added.
61: Increases the target ship's heat by this amount per shot. Only half as effective when the target's shields are up.
62: Reduces the target ship's energy by this amount per shot. Only half as effective when the target's shields are up.
63: Increases the target's ionization by this amount per shot. Only half as effective when the target's shields are up. Ionization reduces the target's energy, and slowly wears off over time.
64: Increases the target's chance of weapon failure. Only half as effective when the target's shields are up. Scrambling slowly wears off over time.
65: Reduces the target's turn rate, acceleration, and top speed. Only half as effective when the target's shields are up. Slowing wears off over time.
66: Allows weapon damage to "leak through" to the hull even if shields are up. Shield disruption wears off over time, and adding additional shield disruption becomes more difficult as damage leaks past shields instead of disrupting them.
67: Shield damage dealt over time by this weapon per shot.
68: Hull damage dealt over time by this weapon per shot.
69: Fuel damage dealt over time by this weapon per shot.
70: Heat damage dealt over time by this weapon per shot.
71: Shield damage dealt per shot, as a percentage of your target's total shield strength.
72: Hull damage dealt per shot, as a percentage of your target's total hull strength.
73: Minable damage dealt as a percentage of the target's total health, in lieu of relative hull damage being used.
74: Fuel loss caused per shot as a percentage of the target's total fuel capacity. Only half as effective when the target's shields are up.
